There is a difference between 'rev limiter', which does exactly as it says and prevents over-revving an engine, but a governor is similar but different. A governor will limit maximum speed no matter what gear you are in. Take the Z06, it's rev limiter is at 7K RPM, but at 6800 RPM in 5th gear it should be doing ~198 MPH. If it had a governor, it would limit the Fuel/RPM to prevent the vehicle from surpassing whatever speed(MPH) wanted, and it wouldn't have to come close to the rev limit. For reference, 6th gear at 3600 RPM is ~160 MPH. Many commercial trucks are governed by the owning company for many reasons including: fuel efficiency, road safety, insurance rates, etc. but this does NOT mean that ALL vehicles have them.
